def-td-thermodynamic-limit-contract.physical_scope: A specified sequence of finite-state macroscopic models at positive temperature with a declared density, interactions, boundary conditions, and normalization; no limiting existence, ensemble equivalence, or critical singularity is asserted.

def-td-thermodynamic-limit-contract:
## Definition

Use $\mathbb N$ from *The natural numbers $\mathbb{N}$ (von Neumann)*, which includes $0$, and define $\mathbb N_{>0}:=\mathbb N\setminus\{0\}$. A **finite-state thermodynamic-limit contract** specifies a sequence $(X_k,E_k,g_k,V_k,n_k)_{k\in\mathbb N_{>0}}$, where each $X_k$ is a finite nonempty state set, $E_k:X_k\to\mathbb R$ assigns finite energies in joules, $g_k:X_k\to(0,\infty)$ assigns positive dimensionless weights, $V_k>0$ is physical volume in $\mathrm{m^3}$, and, for one declared species, $n_k>0$ is its amount in moles. A fixed-density sequence has $V_k\to\infty$ and $n_k/V_k\to\rho\in(0,\infty)$ in $\mathrm{mol\,m^{-3}}$. Boundary conditions, interaction rules, and the choice of a volume or amount normalization are part of the contract and must be held fixed or explicitly tracked as $k$ varies.

For $T>0$, set $\beta:=(k_BT)^{-1}$ in $\mathrm{J^{-1}}$, with $k_B$ and units from *SI quantities and unit conventions*. The finite-state canonical partition sum is

$$
Z_k(\beta):=\sum_{x\in X_k}g_k(x)e^{-\beta E_k(x)},
$$

as the finite case of *Countable canonical model*. It is a positive finite real number. Define $F_k(\beta):=-\beta^{-1}\log Z_k(\beta)$ in joules and $f_k(\beta):=F_k(\beta)/V_k$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. The specified thermodynamic-limit value is $f(\beta,\rho):=\lim_{k\to\infty} f_k(\beta)$ **if this limit exists**. A limit per mole or per lattice site is a different normalization and must be stated separately.

This is a contract for what a limit claim must specify, not a theorem that the limit exists. It asserts no uniformity in $\beta$, derivative interchange, ensemble equivalence, convergence rate, or nonanalyticity. A finite model's regularity and any limiting singularity require their own arguments; neither is inferred from the word “thermodynamic limit.”

pthm-td-fixed-tp-reaction-potential-mini.physical_scope: A closed reacting system at fixed positive reservoir temperature and fixed external pressure, represented by a system process record and an admitted isolated-compound extension with the exact ideal-reservoir, pressure-store, and feasible-set data stated here; no external matter exchange, omitted work channel, nonideal reservoir, or kinetic relaxation claim is included.

pthm-td-fixed-tp-reaction-potential-mini:
## Statement

Fix a closed system $s$ of constitution $c$, with equilibrium domain $D_c$ from *Equilibrium state domains*, and fix $T_0>0$ and $p_0>0$. Define, for $x\in D_c$,
$$
\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x):=U_c(x)+p_0V_c(x)-T_0S_c(x),
$$
where $U_c,V_c$ are the dimensioned energy and volume maps of *Equilibrium state domains* and $S_c$ is the adopted entropy of *Concave macroscopic fundamental entropy*. Thus $\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ has units joules.

Let $P_s\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ be an admitted closed system process record as defined in *Thermodynamic process records and transfer conventions*, with system endpoints $x_{P_s}^-,x_{P_s}^+\in D_c$. Let $R$ be its ideal thermal reservoir and $B$ its ideal pressure store; both lie inside a declared isolated-compound outer boundary. Let $\widehat P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s\sqcup R\sqcup B)$ be an admitted core closed process record for that isolated compound, whose supplied total mass is positive, whose endpoint center-of-mass velocities are defined in one fixed Galilean chart, and whose compound center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change. These are conditions on the whole compound, additional to the system-record conditions. By an extension, require that $\widehat P$ has the same time interval, system endpoints, system configuration path, and system-side protocol and transfer records as $P_s$, together with the reservoir and store records. Write its compound endpoint association as
$$
\rho_{\widehat P}(\pm)=(x_{P_s}^\pm,y_R^\pm,y_B^\pm)\in\mathcal F\subseteq D_c\times Y_R\times Y_B,
$$
where $Y_R,Y_B$ are the model-declared reservoir and store equilibrium state sets, represented as admitted constituent state domains (or subsets thereof) in the second-law endpoint split; $E_R,E_B$ and their entropies are the corresponding dimensioned state maps. The split is admitted as independent separated macroscopic systems by *Concave macroscopic fundamental entropy*. The set $\mathcal F$ is the exact feasible endpoint set from *Isolated compound and feasible equilibrium set*. The system protocol assigns heat $Q[P_s]$ and work $W_{\rm on}[P_s]$ to $P_s$; the auxiliary endpoint changes in $\widehat P$ satisfy the reservoir and store relations in [A1]–[A2] below. No matter crosses the compound boundary, no work channel other than pressure-store work acts on the system, and no other energy-coordinate changes are omitted.

Then the system endpoint difference obeys
$$
\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x_{P_s}^+)-\Phi_{T_0,p_0}(x_{P_s}^-)\le0.
$$
If the final compound endpoint $\rho_{\widehat P}(+)$ is an attained global entropy maximum on $\mathcal F$, then $x_{P_s}^+$ attains a global minimum of $\Phi_{T_0,p_0}$ on the system projection
$$
\Pi_s(\mathcal F):=\{x\in D_c:\exists y_R\in Y_R,\ y_B\in Y_B\text{ with }(x,y_R,y_B)\in\mathcal F\}.
$$
This is a conditional model deduction; it does not assert that arbitrary fixed-$T,p$ reactions have this preparation or that the system reaches the minimum dynamically.

def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain.physical_scope: Model-specified phase branches of nonrelativistic macroscopic thermodynamic systems in positive-temperature, positive-composition, positive-amount charts; intensive scale invariance and same-tag homogeneity are separate branch assumptions, and no branch existence, stability, boundary smoothness, or universal phase rule is asserted.

def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain:
## Definition

Fix a constitution $c$ with $C\ge1$ named species and its equilibrium state domain $D_c\subseteq\mathbb R^{C+2}$ from *Equilibrium state domains*. An interior composition is represented by

$$
x=(x_1,\ldots,x_{C-1})\in\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^{C-1}:x_i>0,\ \sum_{i=1}^{C-1}x_i<1\},
$$

with $x_C:=1-\sum_{i<C}x_i>0$; for $C=1$, $\mathbb R^0=\{0\}$ and $x_1=1$.

A **phase branch** $\alpha$ is model data consisting of an open chart $W_\alpha\subseteq(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}\times(0,\infty)$ with coordinates $(T,p,x,m)$ and a $C^1$ diffeomorphism $\sigma_\alpha:W_\alpha\to U_\alpha$ onto an open subset $U_\alpha\subseteq\mathbb R^{C+2}$ contained in the equilibrium state domain $D_c$. Here $T$ is in kelvins, $p$ is in pascals, $m$ is total amount in moles, and $C^1$ means continuous first coordinate derivatives as in *$C^k$ Euclidean maps and diffeomorphisms*. The chart dimension is $C+2$, matching the ambient dimension of $D_c$. The map $\sigma_\alpha$ takes values in numerical state coordinates; its physical SI state map is explicitly $\chi_\alpha=\Phi_c\circ\sigma_\alpha$, where $\Phi_c$ is the numerical-to-SI unit map of *Entropic temperature, pressure, and molar chemical potentials*. Thus the physical amounts at this point are $n_j=m x_j$, and the numerical amount coordinates in $\sigma_\alpha$ are $n_j/(1\,\mathrm{mol})$. Derivative-defined physical state functions are evaluated on $\chi_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$, or equivalently pulled back along $\Phi_c$ to $\sigma_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$. At $\sigma_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$ in this precise pullback sense, the derivative-defined state functions of *Entropic temperature, pressure, and molar chemical potentials* give temperature $T$, pressure $p$, and mole fractions $x_j=n_j/m$; here $n_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^C n_i=m$ uses the finite-sum convention of *Finite sums and finite products, by recursion*. An **intensive phase branch** additionally has each derivative-defined chemical potential $\mu_j(T,p,x,m)$ independent of $m$ throughout $W_\alpha$; write its value as $\mu_j^\alpha(T,p,x)$. This scale invariance is an explicit constitutive model property, not a consequence of *Additive separated systems and tagged bulk scaling*. A valid local response chart and its inverse are as in *Thermodynamic response functions on valid local charts* and *Local thermodynamic Legendre potentials*. Existence of $W_\alpha$ or $\sigma_\alpha$ is a model premise, not a consequence of the equations of thermodynamics.

On a branch with a valid natural-variable chart, $G^\alpha$ denotes the Gibbs potential of *Local thermodynamic Legendre potentials* restricted to the branch. For a one-component branch with amount $m_\alpha>0$, define $g_\alpha:=G^\alpha/m_\alpha$, $s_\alpha:=S_\alpha/m_\alpha$, and $v_\alpha:=V_\alpha/m_\alpha$, in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, respectively. These quotients need not be independent of amount, and $g_\alpha=\mu^\alpha$ is not assumed by this definition. Such an equality requires a separate same-tag homogeneity hypothesis on the branch.

A **phase mixture** of a finite list of branches is a feasible separated compound whose positive phase amounts $m_\alpha$ have fractions $\lambda_\alpha:=m_\alpha/\sum_\beta m_\beta>0$ with $\sum_\alpha\lambda_\alpha=1$. Its extensive coordinates and entropy are those supplied by *Additive separated systems and tagged bulk scaling* and *Concave macroscopic fundamental entropy*, on the exact feasible set of *Isolated compound and feasible equilibrium set*. The mixture is in **coexistence** when it is an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint under the declared totals and permitted exchanges, as in *Stable equilibrium requires an attained global entropy maximum*. This definition does not assert that a maximum exists, that all branches can exchange every coordinate, or that metastable states are global equilibria.

The bulk scaling postulate may send a material tag $c$ to a different tag $c^{(\lambda)}$. It therefore does not supply same-tag degree-one homogeneity of $G^\alpha$ or $U^\alpha$ on a phase branch. Any result using $g_\alpha=\mu^\alpha$ must state that additional hypothesis.

pthm-td-intensive-coexistence-conditions.physical_scope: Finite coexisting phase branches in positive-temperature C2 charts at an attained global entropy maximum, and only the energy, volume, or species transfers declared pairwise feasible in both directions.

pthm-td-intensive-coexistence-conditions:
## Statement

Let $P\ge1$ named phase branches of the same finite species list occupy a separated compound at an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint with the fixed totals and exact feasible set declared by *Phase branches and coexistence domains* and *Isolated compound and feasible equilibrium set*. Assume each phase lies in an open C2 single-phase chart with finite positive temperature. For every pair of phases, assume the following about the feasible set at this endpoint: each named exchange channel permits a sufficiently small nonzero amount of transfer in both directions, while all other state coordinates may be held fixed.

Then, for every pair $\alpha,\beta$:
- if energy exchange is permitted, $T_\alpha=T_\beta$;
- if volume exchange is permitted, $p_\alpha/T_\alpha=p_\beta/T_\beta$, and if energy exchange is also permitted then $p_\alpha=p_\beta$;
- if species $j$ is transferable, $\mu_{\alpha,j}/T_\alpha=\mu_{\beta,j}/T_\beta$, and if energy exchange is also permitted then $\mu_{\alpha,j}=\mu_{\beta,j}$.

The pressure and chemical potentials are the derivative-defined state functions of *Entropic temperature, pressure, and molar chemical potentials*. The theorem makes no equality claim for a retained coordinate, a one-sided boundary exchange, or a channel absent from the declared feasible set. It is a model deduction, not evidence that these phases or exchange channels occur in nature.

pthm-td-reaction-boundary-equilibrium.physical_scope: Local C1 constrained Gibbs-potential charts for a declared internal reaction network at fixed positive reservoir temperature and pressure; interior conclusions use the admitted process-record model, while boundary conclusions require the explicit boundary-inclusive entropy and auxiliary extension stated here.

pthm-td-reaction-boundary-equilibrium:
## Statement

Fix $C\ge1$ species and $R\ge1$ declared internal reaction extents. Let $\nu\in\mathbb R^{C\times R}$ be the dimensionless stoichiometric matrix, let $n^0\in[0,\infty)^C$ have units mol, and let $\xi\in\mathbb R^R$ have units mol. The amount vector is $n(\xi)=n^0+\nu\xi$, and the nonnegative-amount feasible extent set is
$$
\mathcal F_\nu:=\{\xi\in\mathbb R^R:n^0+\nu\xi\in[0,\infty)^C\}.
$$
Assume the exact local reaction-feasible extent set is $\mathcal F_\nu\cap U$; no additional local constraint removes any direction in its tangent cone.
Fix $T_0>0$ and $p_0>0$ in a declared natural-variable chart. On an open neighborhood $U$ of a candidate endpoint $\xi_*$, let $\Phi:U\to\mathbb R$ be a finite $C^1$ constrained Gibbs-potential extension, in joules, satisfying
$$
D\Phi(\xi)[h]=\sum_{j=1}^C\mu_j(\xi)(\nu h)_j=(\nu^{\mathsf T}\mu(\xi))\cdot h,
$$
where every $\mu_j$ is in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. At positive amounts, require $\Phi(\xi)=U_c(x(\xi))+p_0V_c(x(\xi))-T_0S_c(x(\xi))$ for the system state $x(\xi)$, with $U_c,V_c,S_c$ from *Equilibrium state domains* and *Concave macroscopic fundamental entropy*; its derivative is that of the local Gibbs chart supplied by *Local thermodynamic Legendre potentials* and *Differentials of the thermodynamic potentials*.

If all amounts at $\xi_*$ are positive, assume $\xi_*$ is the system endpoint of a closed system process record and its admitted isolated-compound extension exactly as in *Fixed-temperature and fixed-pressure potential minimum with internal reactions*, is a global entropy-maximizing endpoint on that extension's exact feasible set, and the record's system projection contains every state $x(\xi)$ for $\xi\in\mathcal F_\nu\cap U$. If at least one amount is zero, it is outside *Equilibrium state domains*; in that boundary case, assume instead that the model supplies a boundary-inclusive state domain with finite $C^1$ maps $\bar U_c,\bar V_c,\bar S_c:U\to\mathbb R$ in joules, $\mathrm{m^3}$, and $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, respectively, that $\Phi(\xi)=\bar U_c(\xi)+p_0\bar V_c(\xi)-T_0\bar S_c(\xi)$, and that its exact isolated-compound model has fixed total energy, an ideal reservoir with $S_R(E_R)=S_{R,0}+E_R/T_0$, a constant-entropy pressure store satisfying $E_B-p_0\bar V_c(\xi)=C_B$, and a feasible-set projection equal to $\mathcal F_\nu\cap U$. Assume $\xi_*$ is an attained global entropy maximum on that boundary-inclusive set. This additional boundary model premise is not supplied by the positive-mole state chart or by *Fixed-temperature and fixed-pressure potential minimum with internal reactions*.

Under the relevant interior or boundary assumptions above, $\xi_*$ locally minimizes $\Phi$ on $\mathcal F_\nu\cap U$. Let $J_*:=\{j:n^0_j+(\nu\xi_*)_j=0\}$ be the active species set. Then the first-order necessary condition is
$$
(\nu^{\mathsf T}\mu(\xi_*))\cdot h\ge0\qquad\text{for every }h\in T_{\mathcal F_\nu}(\xi_*),
$$
where
$$
T_{\mathcal F_\nu}(\xi_*):=\{h\in\mathbb R^R:(\nu h)_j\ge0\text{ for every }j\in J_*\}.
$$
If $\xi_*$ is interior to $\mathcal F_\nu$, this reduces to $\nu^{\mathsf T}\mu(\xi_*)=0$. If, in addition, $\Phi$ is convex and differentiable on a convex neighborhood containing the relevant feasible set, the same tangent inequality is sufficient for global minimization there.

pthm-td-clapeyron-local.physical_scope: A one-component, positive-temperature, C1 coexistence branch with bilateral energy, volume, and species exchange, nonzero molar-volume jump, and the explicit local same-tag homogeneity and reversible-heat assumptions stated here, with homogeneity either independently stipulated or supplied on each designated common-law bulk branch through the local Euler theorem; the slope formula requires nonzero molar-volume jump and C1 branch charts and is not asserted when either condition fails.

pthm-td-clapeyron-local:
## Statement

Let $\alpha,\beta$ be two one-component phase branches from *Phase branches and coexistence domains* on a common open chart $O\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ with coordinates $(T,p)$. Assume each branch has a local $C^2$ energy representation $\mathcal U_i(s,V,n)$, $i\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$, and that within each fixed branch tag it satisfies the same-tag homogeneity
$$
\mathcal U_i(\lambda s,\lambda V,\lambda n)=\lambda\mathcal U_i(s,V,n)
$$
for all $\lambda$ in a neighborhood of $1$ for which the scaled state remains in the chart. This is a phase-branch hypothesis: the general tagged law of *Additive separated systems and tagged bulk scaling* does not imply it. It may be stipulated independently on each local branch, or supplied by the common-law bulk subclass of *Euler and Gibbs-Duhem identities under same-tag homogeneity* when each phase's local inverse states lie in its designated entropy cone with fixed species and intensive parameters and common SI units and energy/entropy reference conventions. That supplied subclass uses local inverse uniqueness and does not require a global energy inverse.

Suppose a state $(T_0,p_0)\in O$ is an attained interior coexistence equilibrium with bilateral energy, volume, and species exchange between the two branches, and both branches admit the valid local Gibbs charts of *Local thermodynamic Legendre potentials*. Write $g_i=G_i/n_i$, $s_i=S_i/n_i$, and $v_i=V_i/n_i$ in the units specified by *SI quantities and unit conventions*. If
$$
\Delta v(T_0,p_0):=v_\beta(T_0,p_0)-v_\alpha(T_0,p_0)\ne0,
$$
then, on some open interval about $T_0$, the equal-Gibbs-per-mole coexistence condition $g_\alpha(T,p(T))=g_\beta(T,p(T))$ defines a unique local $C^1$ curve and
$$
\frac{dp}{dT}=\frac{s_\beta-s_\alpha}{v_\beta-v_\alpha}.
$$
If, in addition, conversion from $\alpha$ to $\beta$ is admitted as a reversible process in contact with an ideal thermal reservoir at the same fixed $T$, and the full finite isolated compound (converted phases, reservoir, work stores and all auxiliaries) has equilibrium endpoints with additive component entropy, with every component other than the converted phases and that reservoir having zero entropy change, and the admitted forward and reverse complete-compound records have nonnegative total endpoint entropy changes for that same additive split with their full endpoint tuples interchanged, then its molar latent heat absorbed by the system is $\ell_{\alpha\to\beta}=T(s_\beta-s_\alpha)$. These are conditional model deductions. The slope conclusion is not asserted when $\Delta v=0$ or where the branch charts are not $C^1$.

pthm-td-compact-continuous-phase-mixture.physical_scope: Mixtures of a compact set of declared phase-generator states with continuous entropy and a fixed barycenter; every feasible Borel probability mixture is included, while no attainment claim is made for noncompact domains or a different physical normalization.

pthm-td-compact-continuous-phase-mixture:
## Statement

Let $d\ge1$ and let $K\subseteq\mathbb R^d$ be a nonempty compact set of dimensionless generator coordinates. Each $x\in K$ labels one model-specified phase-generator state; the model assigns it entropy per mole $s(x)\in\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $s:K\to\mathbb R$ is continuous, using the numerical entropy value in that fixed unit. Define $\operatorname{conv}K$ to be the set of all finite convex combinations of points of $K$, and fix $\bar x\in\operatorname{conv}K$. Use the Borel sigma algebra relative to $K$. A Borel probability mixture is a countably additive probability measure $P$ on that sigma algebra; its barycenter and entropy per mole are the coordinatewise integrals $\int_Kx\,dP$ and $\int_Ks\,dP$. For $x\in K$, define the unit point mass $\delta_x$ by $\delta_x(A)=1$ if $x\in A$ and $\delta_x(A)=0$ otherwise, for Borel $A\subseteq K$. Assume every Borel probability mixture with barycenter $\bar x$ is feasible and has entropy per mole $\int_Ks\,dP$. Then there are $m\le d+1$, points $x_1,\ldots,x_m\in K$, and weights $\theta_i\ge0$ with $\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i=1$ such that $P_*:=\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i\delta_{x_i}$ is a feasible Borel probability mixture and $\int_Ks\,dP_*\ge\int_Ks\,dP$ for every feasible mixture $P$.

Here integrals use the measure convention of *Measure space and integral*. The entropy map is part of the model; this theorem derives neither its microscopic meaning nor compactness of a physical phase domain.

pthm-td-regular-gibbs-phase-rule.physical_scope: Interior compositions of finitely many C1 intensive phase branches with energy, volume, all listed species exchanges, and internal reactions allowed in every phase with auxiliary states fixed along the stipulated pairwise transfer curves and vanishing derivative of total auxiliary entropy along each stipulated reaction curve at the coexistence point, at a solution where the combined coexistence-and-affinity Jacobian has a nonsingular minor; phase amounts and externally fixed variables are excluded, and the conclusion is not asserted where a C1 phase chart fails, composition lies on the simplex boundary, or the nonsingular-minor hypothesis fails.

pthm-td-regular-gibbs-phase-rule:
## Statement

Assume the entropy of each phase is $C^2$ on its physical state chart and its derivative-defined temperature at the endpoint is finite and positive. The equation-set dimension below concerns this smooth interior state only.

Let $C\ge1$ be the number of named species, $P\ge1$ the number of coexisting phase branches, and $R\ge0$ the number of independent internal reaction directions. Consider an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint on the exact feasible set of *Isolated compound and feasible equilibrium set*. For each phase $\alpha$, use an intensive phase branch from *Phase branches and coexistence domains* and an interior composition $x^\alpha\in\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}$. Let each branch chemical-potential map
$$
\mu^\alpha(T,p,x^\alpha)=(\mu_1^\alpha,\ldots,\mu_C^\alpha)
$$
be $C^1$ on a common open domain
$$
\mathcal U=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times(\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ})^P \subseteq\mathbb R^{\,n},\qquad n=2+P(C-1).
$$
Let $\nu^1,\ldots,\nu^R\in\mathbb R^C$ be linearly independent, dimensionless stoichiometric vectors, with extents measured in moles. Assume that, for every phase pair and each of energy, volume, and every named species, the feasible set contains the pairwise transfer curve for all sufficiently small transfers of either sign, varying only the selected coordinate in those two phases with opposite increments and holding every other state coordinate of both phases, all other phases, and all auxiliaries fixed. For each phase $\alpha$ and reaction $r$, assume the feasible set contains the complete endpoint curve with species amounts $n^\alpha(t)=n^{\alpha,*}+t\nu^r$ for all sufficiently small extents $t$ of either sign, while that phase's energy and volume, all other reaction extents, and every other phase's state remain fixed at their coexistence values. Require the total entropy contribution of all retained auxiliaries along each such reaction curve to be differentiable at zero extent with derivative zero. Every auxiliary state may be fixed as a sufficient special case, but entropy-neutral varying auxiliary or work-device states are permitted. Phase equilibrium imposes $\mu_i^\alpha-\mu_i^1=0$ for $1\le i\le C$, $2\le\alpha\le P$; internal reaction equilibrium imposes $(\nu^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha=0$ in every phase for $1\le r\le R$. On the phase-equality locus these are the same $R$ equations in each phase, so count them once using phase 1. Put $q:=C(P-1)$ and $m:=q+R$. If $m=0$ (equivalently $P=1,R=0$), no equation is imposed and the local zero set is the whole chart, of dimension $n=C+1=C-P+2-R$. If $m\ge1$ and the combined equation map has an invertible $m\times m$ derivative minor at the solution, with $m\le n$, then the local zero set of these first-order coexistence-and-affinity equations is a graph of dimension
$$
n-q-R=C-P+2-R.
$$
This is the dimension of the equation zero set in intensive coordinates only; phase amounts and their extensive conservation constraints are not counted, and the actual stable-coexistence set may be a proper subset after additional stability constraints. If the nonsingular-minor condition fails, no dimension formula is asserted.

rem-td-nonsmooth-phase-scope.physical_scope: Interpretive limits for the phase-branch, coexistence, Clapeyron, and compact-mixture statements on this page; this remark establishes no universal critical or thermodynamic-limit result.

ex-td-finite-two-state-partition-smooth.physical_scope: A constructed two-state canonical model at finite positive temperature; the formulas are model predictions, not measured material properties or a thermodynamic-limit result.

ex-td-vdw-positive-slope.physical_scope: An exact derivative calculation in the dimensionless reduced van der Waals model below its model critical temperature; no real-fluid measurement or universal equation of state is asserted.

ex-td-phase-fraction-lever-rule.physical_scope: A constructed one-component, two-phase separated mixture with additive volume and fixed total amount; no coexistence data or measured material values are asserted.

ex-td-reaction-boundary-example.physical_scope: A constructed units-labelled tangent-cone optimization illustration with one zero-amount boundary; it makes no thermodynamic-equilibrium, material, or empirical claim.

cex-td-noncompact-phase-mixture-no-attai.physical_scope: A constructed continuous entropy extension that is positive and concave on a convex ambient domain but restricted to a noncompact generator set omitting its maximizing barycenter; it makes no material claim.

ex-td-compact-continuous-phase-mixture.physical_scope: A constructed finite two-generator mixture with a continuous concave entropy functional; its values are illustrative and are not observations.

ex-td-clapeyron-linear-branches.physical_scope: A constructed pair of one-component Gibbs charts satisfying the same-tag, exchange, and reversible-heat assumptions with core closed forward and reverse compound records of the local Clapeyron theorem; the constants are illustrative and are not observations.

cex-td-clapeyron-zero-volume-jump.physical_scope: A constructed pair of smooth one-component Gibbs charts with zero molar-volume jump; it shows why the local nonzero-jump hypothesis cannot be omitted and makes no material claim.

ex-td-phase-rule-single-component.physical_scope: A constructed pair of smooth one-component Gibbs charts; the example verifies the regular equation-set rank and dimension only, and does not assert a stable or realized coexistence endpoint.

ex-td-reactive-phase-rule-three-componen.physical_scope: A constructed smooth local two-phase Gibbs model with one formal internal reaction, used to verify the local equation-map nonsingular-minor hypothesis only; no stable or realized coexistence claim, empirical system, or chemical data are made.
